fuel_basis: GE identifies both turbine types as gas turbines (PGT25+G4 generator sets; LM6000-PF+ mechanical-drive units) supplied specifically for FLNG Dua's liquefaction/compression and power-generation duty; standard aeroderivative gas-turbine technology run on fuel gas aboard FLNG facilities.
captive_summary: PFLNG DUA (Dua FLNG Terminal), a moored offshore FLNG vessel, carries 4x PGT25+G4 gas turbine generator systems supplying the facility's electric power and 2x LM6000-PF+ 2BCL907 aeroderivative gas turbines mechanically driving the nitrogen liquefaction-train compressors. Both were installed under GE Oil & Gas's November 2014 turbomachinery contract for FLNG Dua.

Corroborated independently by offshore-technology.com's project profile of PFLNG DUA, which repeats the identical equipment description.

captive_summary: No public source describes an on-site/captive power arrangement for RGT Kemaman (E&H Energy's proposed LNG import/regas terminal at Teluk Kalong, Kemaman). The project is still pre-construction -- as of mid-2026 it was awaiting the 'Letter to Proceed' targeted for Q2 2026 -- and no EIA, design filing, or technical release addressing electricity supply has surfaced.
confirmed_how: Reviewed E&H Energy project coverage (thesun.my, dagangnews.com, evolusibina.com, Terengganu Inc. investment pages) and searched for a Malaysian DOE EIA filing; none disclose a power-generation arrangement for the terminal itself. RM3.7bn RGT Kemaman is described as ~3.6 Mtpa initial capacity (expandable to 5 Mtpa), targeted 2028-2029 start, still at pre-Letter-to-Proceed stage as of 2026 -- consistent with design details (including any captive power) not yet being public.
gogpt_prior_assessment: The GOGPT prior (Eastern Steel Kemaman plant power station, 155 MW, gogpt_captive=True, 5.14 km away) is Eastern Steel's OWN captive power plant serving its integrated steel mill (coke/sintering/iron-and-steel-making) at Teluk Kalong -- a different industrial host in the same industrial area, unrelated to and not built to serve E&H Energy's LNG terminal. Eastern Steel's own site lists 'power generation' as one of its integrated production processes. https://www.easternsteel.com.my/en/about.html
gogpt_candidate_basis: GOGPT record already exists (Eastern Steel Kemaman plant power station) and it is unrelated to this LNG terminal -- different owner/host (steel mill vs. E&H Energy's regas terminal); no evidence this terminal has or will have its own captive generation.
status_or_other_findings: RGT Kemaman: RM3.7bn (~3.6 Mtpa initial, expandable to 5 Mtpa) LNG import/regas terminal at Teluk Kalong, Kemaman; E&H Energy has secured 6 Mtpa LNG supply from 2028; targeted completion ~2028-2029; as of mid-2026 awaiting Letter to Proceed (targeted Q2 2026). Informational only, not staged.

captive_summary: The cancelled Regasification Terminal Lahad Datu (RTLD) project -- a 2012 JV between Petronas Gas (80%) and Sabah Energy (20%), 0.76 mtpa capacity, terminated Feb 2016 -- was designed to supply gas to an ADJACENT 300MW combined-cycle power plant, not to power itself. This is the opposite (PowerPlantsSupplied) direction, not a captive-power relationship, and the project never reached FID/construction, so no on-site generation design was ever published.
confirmed_how: Two independent trade-press outlets reporting the 2016 termination both state: 'The LNG terminal planned to supply gas to an adjacent 300MW combined cycle power plant in Lahad Datu, Sabah' (offshore-technology.com) / 'an adjacent 300MW combined cycle power plant in the town of Lahad Datu, Sabah' (offshore-energy.biz) -- confirming the terminal's function was fuel supply OUT to a separate power station, the reverse of a captive-power relationship. Both also confirm the JV was mutually terminated 10 Feb 2016 after 'prolonged uncertainty' (the project had been on hold since the Feb 2013 Lahad Datu armed intrusion).

hardware_summary: GE-supplied gas turbines comprising both the plant's power-generation units and its liquefaction-train (refrigerant compressor) drivers across the Bintulu complex (MLNG, MLNG Dua, MLNG Tiga). Pre-2024 the complex relied 'solely on gas-powered turbines' for electricity; a 2024 grid tie-in (Project GLORY) substitutes only 40% (90 MW) of PLC's total power requirement with Sarawak-hydro electricity, leaving the remaining majority of house power gas-turbine-generated. Train-specific Frame-turbine models/ratings for MLNG Dua were not found in a citable primary source this pass.
fuel_basis: Petronas's own account: 'instead of relying solely on gas-powered turbines, PLC will be supplied partially with electricity generated by hydropower' -- establishing the pre-existing/continuing power source as gas-turbine combustion. GE's press release groups the equipment it services as 'gas turbines and related equipment that comprise the power generation units and liquefaction trains for the LNG complex.'
captive_summary: The PETRONAS LNG Complex (PLC) at Bintulu -- which includes MLNG Dua (Trains 4-6) -- generates its own electricity on gas-fired turbines. Petronas's own 2024 account states the complex was 'relying solely on gas-powered turbines' for power before a new 90 MW grid tie-in (Project GLORY, completed ~Q4 2024) substituted 40% of total site demand with Sarawak hydro-electricity, leaving the majority still gas-turbine generated. GE's separate service-contract press release confirms its maintained gas turbines 'comprise the power generation units and liquefaction trains' across MLNG, MLNG Dua and MLNG Tiga -- i.e. both electricity generation and mechanical-drive compressor trains.
mechanical_drive_note: GE's gas turbines also drive the liquefaction (refrigerant compressor) trains complex-wide per the same GE press release ('liquefaction trains'); no per-train Frame-turbine model or shaft-power figure for MLNG Dua specifically was found in a citable primary source this pass.
confirmed_how: (1) PETRONAS FLOW (petronas.com, Petronas's own publication, 29 Aug 2024): 'The PETRONAS LNG Complex (PLC) - operated by Malaysia LNG Sdn Bhd (MLNG)... instead of relying solely on gas-powered turbines, PLC will be supplied partially with electricity generated by hydropower from the Sarawak main grid... This will supply 90 megawatts of electricity to power the MLNG plants... substitute 40 per cent of PLC's total power requirements.' (2) GE press release announcing its $127.6M LNG-complex service contract: 'It includes all GE-supplied gas turbines and related equipment that comprise the power generation units and liquefaction trains for the LNG complex,' explicitly covering MLNG, MLNG Dua and MLNG Tiga. (3) LNG Prime (independent trade press) corroborates the 90 MW Sarawak Energy/SESCO grid-tie deal to PLC.

This is Sarawak Energy's own regional gas-fired combined-cycle merchant/grid power station at Tanjung Kidurong, Bintulu -- a public utility asset, not built to serve or owned by Malaysia LNG Dua. Independent confirmation: NS Energy Business project profile identifies Sarawak Energy as operator of the Tanjung Kidurong combined-cycle plant. https://www.nsenergybusiness.com/projects/tanjung-kidurong-combined-cycle-power-project/ -- GOGPT's own gogpt_captive=False flag agrees; it correctly already treats Tanjung Kidurong as non-captive.
gogpt_candidate_basis: On-site gas-turbine electricity generation for house power is documented (Petronas/GE), but no source discloses a citable aggregate nameplate MW for the gas-turbine-generating portion specifically -- only the 90 MW/40%-substituted-by-grid figure is known, from which the gas-turbine-generated share (~135 MW implied) could only be derived/inferred, not directly cited.
status_or_other_findings: PLC electrification (Project GLORY): 90 MW grid tie-in from Sarawak Energy/SESCO completed ~Q4 2024, substituting ~40% of total site power demand with hydro electricity. Not a GEM data field but potentially useful researcher_notes context.
notes: Finding is complex-wide (Petronas's own account describes 'PLC' as a whole, not per-train) and applies equally to this terminal's sibling GEM record MLNG Satu LNG Terminal (T100000130294, see below), and by the same logic to MLNG Tiga (T100000130295, not in this shard, already carrying a pre-existing CaptiveGasPower=True) -- consistent findings across the whole Bintulu complex.
